title: I’m making a city builder with dating sim elements. Here’s a little Halloween look at the current build 🎃
author: Kiko_Production
selftext:
Halloween seemed like a good excuse to share some gameplay from City Paradise!  
You build a town, get to know the people running it, and help them out with their work. This clip shows a bit of construction, a visit to city hall, and a game you can play on your in-game phone.  
There’s also a late-night radio shift with Maxima, our robot radio host. That’s where the flashlight comes in.  
Still a work in progress, but I’d love to hear what you think!

comments.author: LocalEmergency5551
comments.body: Looks fun i be happy to tester or play the game

comments.author: WWEtrump
comments.body: the in-game phone idea is cute,and the robot radio host gives it a lot of personality. how are you keeping scale consistent across the buildings and characters? all my units come out of one blender python script and it still fights me

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body: Thanks! What fixed it for me was picking one ruler: the door of my admin building. Every building goes through a small Blender Python kit that uses the same numbers for door, wall and window heights, so nothing gets its own scale. Residents get one uniform scale factor, calibrated so they fit through that door, and I never scale the head and body separately. Interiors are the one cheat: rooms are almost twice the scale of the town outside, because a town seen from above and a room you walk around in want different sizes.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body: Looks like a project that lacks direction.

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body: Why do you think so? I’d be very glad to hear your thoughts.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Because it seems to be an accumulation of half-baked concepts rather than one strong concept?

Like... you say city builder and dating sim. Okay, that's interesting; I can see how those things would go together well.

Then you show a city builder with one pretty nice and specific aesthetic that turns into... a first-person adventure game? Then into a game with some bad-looking minigame? Then into a FNAF clone, because God knows we need another FNAF clone in the world?

...Like, where is the promised city builder/dating sim? This is a handful of concepts stapled together with no sense of aesthetic or mechanical cohesion.

  
EDIT: I called this a collection of half-baked concepts. That's an unfair characterization; a collection is a well-curated selection of things that complement and contextualize each other. 

This is just an accumulation. The equivalent of a horde of old cassette tapes, AV cables and spare parts for long-departed appliances.

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body: Hahaha that makes sense, I’ll think about it. Thank you.

replies.author: Kiko_Production
replies.body: Maybe I’ll move forward with a more character-driven city builder concept, where city management remains the main focus, while interacting with characters, exploring their stories, and playing minigames are optional side activities. I think that better reflects what I’m actually trying to make.

replies.author: OkBet5427
replies.body: Yup I can see its all over the place the art style and even the game play 🥲
